title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 175
paragraphs: When the Greeks had returned to the Isthmus, they deliberated, in the light of what Alexander had said, where and in what places they should make their stand. The opinion that prevailed was to guard the pass at Thermopylae: it was seen to be narrower than the one leading into Thessaly, and at the same time it was a single pass and also nearer their own country. As for the path by which those of the Greeks who were taken by the enemy at Thermopylae were captured, they did not even know of its existence until they were told of it by the people of Trachis after they had arrived at Thermopylae. This pass, then, they resolved to guard, and not to allow the barbarian to pass into Greece. They also resolved that the fleet should sail to Artemisium in the territory of Histiaea, for these two positions are close to one another, so that each division could have information of what was happening to the other. The places are situated as I shall describe.
